lines.text: After Jehoshaphat returned safely to Jerusalem, Jehu son of Hanani rebuked him for helping the wicked, yet noted he had removed the Asherah poles.
Jehoshaphat went out among the people from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim and turned them back to the LORD.
Jehoshaphat appointed judges in each fortified city of Judah and told them they were judging for the king, not for man.
In Jerusalem he appointed Levites, priests, and family heads to judge disputes and warn people so they would not incur guilt.
Jehoshaphat said Zebadiah the chief priest would be over all that pertains to the LORD, and Amariah over the king's matters.
